title: The Story of the River Ganga
captions: After the yajna, the sages said, “King Janaka of Mithila is holding a great yajna. Come and see the mighty bow he keeps there.” So the princes set out with Vishvamitra, and in time they reached the holy river Ganga.
Rama looked at the sparkling water and asked, “Great sage, how did the Ganga come to flow on the earth?” The princes sat close to their teacher and listened carefully.

“Long ago,” said the sage, “your ancestor King Sagara of Ayodhya began a great yajna with a sacred horse. But the horse vanished! His sixty thousand sons searched the whole earth and dug deep below it.”
“At last they found the horse beside the great sage Kapila, who sat in peace. Thinking he was the thief, they rushed at him in anger. With one mighty sound, the sage turned them all to ashes.”
“Only the holy Ganga, flowing down from heaven, could bring peace to their souls. Sagara's great great grandson, King Bhagiratha, prayed for many long years, until Lord Brahma granted his wish.”
“But Ganga's fall was so mighty that it could break the earth. So Lord Shiva stood on the mountain and caught her in his matted hair. Then, at Bhagiratha's prayer, he gently let her flow out.”
“Ganga followed Bhagiratha's chariot all the way to the ashes, and her holy water set the sons of Sagara free. That is why she is also called Bhagirathi.” The princes listened in wonder.
lesson: When Rama asked about the river, he did not rush on. He and Lakshmana sat close to their teacher and listened with full attention, and through listening they learned the story of their own ancestors and of King Bhagiratha, who never gave up. In our tradition, Shravana, careful listening, is the first step of all learning. The wisdom of the Vedas was kept alive for thousands of years by people who listened well and remembered.
card_lesson: Rama and Lakshmana sat close to their teacher and listened with full attention. Shravana means listening carefully, so that what we hear can become wisdom in our hearts.
question: Who tells you stories about our family or our traditions? What is one story you remember well?
